page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng tests, alongside average single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, multi-core scaling is limited, with multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, as indicated by a poor PassMark memory score in the bottom 10% and low read/write bandwidths.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as an entry-level compute-focused option. It provides dedicated AMD EPYC execution resources without the overhead of excess memory. Due to the limited 8.0 GB RAM capacity and weak multi-core scaling, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or medium-sized language model inference. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale utility workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation but require minimal memory overhead.
